sin.name: python-blocked-await
sin.description: `time.sleep`, `requests.get` or `subprocess.run` inside an `async def` — the thread it stops is the event loop, so every coroutine waiting on it stops too
sin.rule: A coroutine never stops its own thread: await the asynchronous counterpart, or hand the blocking work to a thread.
sin.suggestion: Use the asynchronous form and `await` it (`asyncio.sleep`, an async client), or `await asyncio.to_thread(...)` when only a blocking call exists. Stopping the loop here is what makes the slowdown appear under load and nowhere else.
